# 薪資與聯準會異議發言，推升月底美債殖利率

## 實質殖利率帶動新一波全面賣壓

就業成本偏強、聯準會三名異議官員質疑等待的理由，美債週五全線下跌。2年期殖利率升5個基點至4.28%，5年期與10年期各升7個基點至4.45%、4.75%，30年期升6個基點至5.27%。這次短端也加入賣壓，不再是週三短債反彈、長債下跌的分裂。

第2季就業成本增加0.9%，高於市場預估中位數。聯準會本週以9比3維持利率在3.5%至3.75%；投下反對票的克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack、明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari及達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan，週五分別解釋為何主張升息25個基點。他們擔心，若現在緊縮不足，日後可能被迫採取更大幅度的行動。油價再度上漲、歐元區通膨升溫，也使投資人更難忽視這些警告。

美國10年期殖利率升幅主要來自實質殖利率，後者升6個基點至2.47%，通膨補償僅升1個基點至2.28%。股票上漲、高收益基金近乎持平、美元走弱，壓力集中在持有存續期間所需的報酬，而非全面搶流動性。但較弱借款人已暴露出股市改善無法解決的問題：Cable One難以籌資完成強制收購，Extenet則在現金與擔保品控管被指失效之際，未付債息。

## 短端重新加入長債的價格調整

賣壓由2至5年期開始，逐步向外延伸。5年期、10年期升幅略大，額外轉陡卻有限，2s10s擴大2個基點至47，2s30s擴大1個基點至99。單日曲線變化不大，整月損失卻很重：7月2年期殖利率升14個基點，5年期升26，10年期升31，30年期升36。

三名異議官員更清楚表達理由。Hammack認為政策抑制力不夠，Kashkari支持在數據持續到來時逐步緊縮，Logan則認為現在小幅行動，可減少日後更急遽升息的需要。即使考量供給衝擊及生產力，Logan預期通膨也只是朝約2.5%靠攏，而非2%。依他們判斷，支出、勞動需求及金融條件還不足以完成回到目標的最後一段。

就業成本指數增加0.9%，本身並不代表薪資重新加速，但也沒有延續6月PCE物價月減0.1%所帶來的寬慰。對期待聯準會繼續觀望的投資人而言，這不是有利的數據。WTI上漲1.29%至$84.67、布蘭特上漲1.22%至$90.12，則在週末前再添能源通膨壓力。

抗通膨債顯示，實質報酬要求的變化大於平均通膨預期。10年期實質殖利率升6個基點至2.47%，5年期升5至2.19%，30年期升5至3.03%。10年期損益兩平通膨率收2.28%，單日升1個基點、7月僅升4個基點；實質殖利率整月升27個基點，占名目31個基點升幅的大部分。市場仍擔心通膨，但沒有把預期通膨的永久升幅定得同樣大。

成交十分活躍。美債現券交易面額達$1.92兆，增32.4%，名目付息券增33.4%至$1.52兆。7至10年期成交增56.4%至$2,790億，5至7年期近乎倍增至$1,730億，TIPS增191%至$1,212億。這些是雙向成交、不是淨流量，但顯示指標年期與實質殖利率調整發生在活躍市場。

30年期殖利率盤中一度升至5.28%，尾盤指數再平衡買盤才使跌勢略為收斂。長天期美債指數仍單日下跌0.69%、7月下跌3.87%；相較之下，1至3年期美債週五僅跌0.04%，整月仍有0.17%的正報酬。

投資人也為下跌保障付更多錢。1個月、25 delta賣權相對買權的溢價，達約五個月最高，結構瞄準10年期殖利率4.8%至4.9%、30年期5.3%至5.42%。MOVE相對平靜，使偏向下行風險的昂貴保障，比整體利率波動水準更醒目。

下一項供給事件是8至10月季度再融資。標售規模預期不變，焦點在2027年可能增加付息券的指引。另一方面，財政部探索把近$1兆現金餘額的一部分，投入約$13兆附買回市場。若準備金減少，可平滑交割、繳稅及申報期壓力，但作業需求、交易商容量及預估報酬有限，使採用仍不確定。這處理的是資金波動，不是投資人最終可能須買進的額外存續期間。

## Cable One與Extenet暴露不同弱點

Cable One即使討論約12%殖利率，收購義務仍愈來愈難融資。GTCR行使賣回權後，公司須為強制買進Mega Broadband Investments剩餘55%，以及延長債務，募集約$10億。部分既有第一順位貸款殖利率已近18%。

潛在貸款人要求風險隔離，防止母公司補貼Mega Broadband龐大義務。Cable One已有至少$30億長債、自由現金流有限，住宅寬頻競爭又強。核心談判在於新資金能否免受收購負債牽連，而不只是多高殖利率能吸引買方。

Extenet則從展期談判，走到實際漏付。約$5億資產擔保證券7月27日應付利息未支付。付款管理人另表示，原應給債權人的收款流向其他地方，部分擔保權也不再具備對抗第三人的效力。公司仍談判利息暫緩，但被指出的控管問題，不只影響何時收款，也影響能回收多少。

Extenet的現金危機來得比收入惡化更快。營收原本僅小幅下降，公司卻在6月警告，現金可能幾天內就會用罄。這類以光纖、小型基地台及5G設施為基礎的證券，原本以穩定現金流和擔保權吸引投資人；如今債權人面對的關鍵，卻是收入能否流入指定帳戶，以及擔保權能否有效執行。

市政債面對更廣泛的供給與存續期間問題。截至週四指數跌1.72%，可能成為2003年以來最差7月，即使夏季通常有付息及還本支持需求。發行約$470億，高於正常7月速度，同時長美債殖利率接近19年高點，相對估值降到今年較便宜水準。

後續供給也未停歇。醫院今年已發行約$267億債券，Northwell Healthcare仍考慮透過紐約州宿舍管理局發行最多$8億免稅債。在這個疲弱月份之後，這筆潛在的大型發行將再度考驗市場需求。

更廣的企業供給背景也有利貸款人。美國今年非投資級發行接近$2,000億，比2025年同期高約9%；投資級增加三分之一至$1.3兆。槓桿貸款均價從1月97降至95.3，2028年前約$2,400億到期。本週稍早CoreWeave、Proofpoint接受較高利差及更強保障，正是這項變化的例子。

能源大廠則利用高油價帶來的現金流減債。Exxon第2季淨債務減少逾$70億，Chevron以創紀錄的$84億償還債務，Shell淨債務減少約$108億。增加其他借款人負擔的能源漲勢，反而改善了這些公司的資產負債表。

整體信用市場當日表現相對穩健，LQD跌0.15%、HYG漲0.01%、JNK漲0.02%。長天期AAA至A及BBB企業債指數分別跌0.29%、0.25%，跌幅小於長天期美債的0.69%，但整月仍各跌4.58%、4.19%。與這些指數的相對韌性相比，Cable One和Extenet的困境更集中在個別借款人的融資條件與債權保障。

## 歐洲通膨升溫，日本銀行保留後續升息空間

歐元區7月通膨由2.8%加快至2.9%，能源漲10%，服務及排除食品燃料的指標都增強。德國10年期殖利率升1個基點至3.16%。市場仍給予ECB 9月升息25個基點90%的機率，年底前計入42個基點。

法國顯示能源之外的壓力。通膨升至2.4%，高於所有受訪預測及2.0%中位數；服務由1.9%加快至2.3%。歐元區第2季成長已達預估兩倍、一年多來最強，進一步緊縮的成長阻力因此較小。

日本銀行6月升息後，8比1維持1%，但植田和男清楚表示，9月起各次會議都可能行動。基礎通膨接近2%，向上意外的代價更高，金融條件若仍太寬鬆，升息速度可加快。交換市場10月升息機率89%，更早行動仍有可能，但央行沒有承諾9月。

日本數據並不一致。東京排除生鮮食品CPI年增1.9%，預估1.8%；整體及排除生鮮食品、能源的指標均2%，服務微升至1.2%。6月工業生產月增1.3%，零售卻月減4.1%、年增僅0.5%。日本銀行把財政年度成長預測升至0.6%，因補貼而將通膨預測從2.8%降至2.5%。

干預在匯率上爭取時間。週四行動估計JPY8.45兆、約$528億，曾使日圓最多升3.3%。週五再傳第二次操作、紐約聯準銀行詢價及美國財政部協調，日圓升約1.3%至157.28。更強日圓可緩解進口通膨，但干預與預期國內利率提高，也影響購買外國債券的資源及誘因。日本1%政策利率仍遠低於美國區間。

英國能源風險則延伸至前一日偏鴿指引之外。央行首席經濟學家Huw Pill警告，商品波動可能持續到2027年。主要預測為年底通膨峰值3.2%，不利情境在2027年達4.5%，需要比現有3.75%明顯更高的利率。能源已比戰前貴20%，反對立即升息，不代表排除更長期政策風險。

中國債市可能增加一項避險工具。香港準備重新推出5年期中國公債期貨，合約CNY50萬、現金結算，先前2017年及2024年嘗試未能建立持久交易。外資持有境內政府債，已從2017年中約CNY4,500億，增至CNY2兆。能否可靠運用於曲線、基差及附買回相關策略，取決於流動性持續，而非上市本身。

## 哥倫比亞暫停升息，Pemex仍未擺脫政府支持

哥倫比亞維持12%，出乎多數經濟學家預期。27名受訪者中23名預測升息；董事會四票不動、三票升50個基點，另宣布最多累積$40億外匯準備。今年披索升近20%，降低進口通膨、提供等待空間，但買匯可能削弱這項匯率支持。

通膨仍逾6%，目標3%、容忍上下1個百分點。擴張財政、最低工資升23%，以及食品能源衝擊，使壓力偏高，獨立財政委員會預期赤字逾GDP的7%。總裁Leonardo Villar保留再升息，新政府之下，9月將檢驗匯率強勢能否繼續抵銷這些壓力。

南非殖利率則是部分復甦，不是回到戰前。10年期約8.7%，低於伊朗戰爭初期9.5%，仍高於戰前約8%。央行在5月升息取得耐心空間後，維持7%；6月通膨5%，仍超過新3%目標，政策依賴的是對衝擊會消退的信心。

Pemex較好的季度表現，沒有恢復財務獨立。公司獲利MXN180億、約$10億，原油及凝析油產量增1.7%至每日166萬桶，債務仍$775億。政府今年已編列$140億債務支持，惠譽卻估年底前另有$100億營運缺口。

墨西哥財長排除今年再增加政府資金，Pemex仍討論2027年預算與可能再融資。產量約為歷史高點一半，國際夥伴承諾又慢。高油價改善現金流，未消除國家可能承接的融資負擔。

市場管道也取決於操作規則。菲律賓在預期納入摩根大通指數前，計畫從本幣債定價中移除20%扣繳稅影響，讓$2,300億市場接近全球慣例。但在到期前賣出的既有持有人，可能承受市值損失。

印度指數時程卻往後移。免除扣繳與資本利得稅後，6月5日以來約$50億流入合格債券；但不同投資人地區的實施尚未完成，彭博延後納入全球綜合指數。10年期殖利率升3個基點至6.84%，交易員預期再調整5至10個基點。稅改帶來流入，未換來立即入指。

羅馬尼亞勉強保住投資級。申覆及政府補充資料後，惠譽維持BBB-、展望負向。赤字預期從2024年逾GDP的9%降至6%以下，但政治不確定性與2028年選舉，威脅進一步整頓。評等保留融資管道，未取消財政警告。

EMB跌0.14%，15年期以上美元主權債指數跌0.21%，美元指數卻跌0.21%至99.80。匯率未顯示普遍缺美元，但10年期美債4.75%、長債5.27%，仍提高長天期美元現金流的折現負擔。

## 利率衝擊之下，股票仍上漲

S&P 500漲0.70%、Nasdaq 100漲0.60%，VIX降6.44%至15.99。半導體只微升0.07%，一週仍跌4.30%、一個月跌20.61%。大盤風險偏好保持，AI族群卻尚未有足以消除支出回報疑慮的反彈。

WTI、布蘭特各漲1.29%、1.22%，至$84.67、$90.12，整週仍跌，一個月卻都高逾21%。油價增加通膨壓力，但實質殖利率升幅更大，顯示美債故事不只來自石油。

黃金跌1.24%至$4,049.10，美元指數降至99.80，部分因支持日圓的行動。黃金與波動率下降、股票上漲，並不像信心全面瓦解。市場重估實質存續期間及政策不確定性，同時股債交易仍正常運作。

## 下一個焦點：非農就業與季度再融資

8月7日就業報告，接在就業成本增0.9%之後。調查中位數預期新增85,000人、6月為57,000人，失業率維持4.2%。招聘更強，會支持異議官員認為政策抑制不足；就業較弱、後續價格放慢，則有利耐心。實質殖利率可顯示喘息是否超越通膨補償下降。

8至10月季度再融資，把供給預期與聯準會辯論分開。標售規模預期不變，關鍵是指引延後增加，還是為2027年更大發行鋪路。10年期殖利率4.9%、30年期5.3%至5.42%附近的避險，提供市場如何防範更早供給訊號的參考。財政部可能投入附買回，則處理不同年期問題：可平滑交割資金，不能解決付息券承接。

8月歐元區通膨，將顯示7月能源漲10%是否進一步傳到服務，影響9月ECB會議。日本銀行9月18日決策前，則須觀察日圓穩定能否不靠重複干預，或另一波失序日本公債走勢。信用方面，Cable One後續融資、Northwell擬議市政債及AI、軟體交易，將顯示讓利與可執行保障能維持多少管道。延誤或更多風險隔離要求，意味高實質利率正影響更多借款人，即使還不是全面融資中斷。

overall_summary.headline: 薪資與聯準會異議發言，推升月底美債殖利率
overall_summary.session_narrative:
第2季就業成本增加0.9%、高於預期，三名聯準會異議官員也說明為何支持提早緊縮，美債各年期全面下跌。2年期殖利率升5個基點至4.28%，10年期升7個基點至4.75%，30年期升6個基點至5.27%。10年期實質殖利率升6個基點至2.47%，通膨補償則僅升1個基點至2.28%。

放眼整個7月，10年期實質殖利率累計上升27個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅升4個基點。投資人要求更高的實質報酬，是這個月長債承壓的主因。油價及歐洲通膨升溫再添壓力；季度再融資公告前，美債成交活躍，防範債價下跌的避險成本也提高。

融資壓力仍集中在部分借款人。Cable One即使討論雙位數殖利率，仍難籌得強制收購所需資金；Extenet未付債息，付款管理人另指出現金及擔保權問題。市政債面對沉重供給，能源大廠卻利用現金流還債。海外方面，日本銀行維持1%利率但指引偏鷹，哥倫比亞意外維持12%；美元走弱，仍未抵銷美債殖利率上升對新興市場美元債的壓力。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Wages and Fed dissenters send Treasury yields higher into month-end

## Real yields drive another broad bond selloff

Treasuries sold off across the curve on Friday as firm employment costs and the Fed's three dissenters challenged the case for waiting. Two-year yields rose 5 basis points to 4.28%, five- and ten-year yields each climbed 7 to 4.45% and 4.75%, and the 30-year added 6 to 5.27%. Unlike Wednesday's split between a rallying front end and falling long bonds, this time shorter maturities joined the selloff.

Second-quarter employment costs rose 0.9%, above the median forecast. Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari and Dallas's Lorie Logan each explained why they had favored a quarter-point increase rather than the Fed's 9–3 hold at 3.5%–3.75%. Their concern was that insufficient restraint now could require more later. A renewed rise in oil and stronger euro-area inflation added to that argument.

Most of the US ten-year move came through real yields, which rose 6 basis points to 2.47%; breakevens edged up just 1 to 2.28%. Stocks advanced, high-yield funds were almost unchanged and the dollar weakened. The pressure was concentrated in the return required to hold duration, not a general scramble for liquidity. At weaker borrowers, however, expensive money was exposing problems that a better equity market could not solve: Cable One struggled to fund a mandatory acquisition and Extenet missed interest amid reported failures of collateral and cash controls.

## The front end rejoins the long-bond repricing

The selloff started in two- to five-year debt and spread outward. The slightly larger rises at five and ten years produced only modest additional steepening: 2s10s widened 2 basis points to 47 and 2s30s widened 1 to 99. Those small daily curve changes sat on top of a severe month. July yield increases were 14 basis points at two years, 26 at five, 31 at ten and 36 at 30.

The dissenters made their objections more explicit. Hammack said policy was not restrictive enough; Kashkari supported incremental tightening while more data arrived; Logan argued that modest action now could reduce the need for sharper increases later. Even allowing for supply shocks and productivity, Logan saw inflation heading toward roughly 2.5% rather than 2%. Spending, labor demand and financial conditions were not yet doing enough to finish the return to target, in their assessment.

The 0.9% increase in the Employment Cost Index did not by itself establish renewed wage acceleration. But it was the wrong direction for investors looking for confirmation of patience after June PCE prices fell 0.1%. WTI's 1.29% rise to $84.67 and Brent's 1.22% gain to $90.12 added energy pressure ahead of the weekend.

Inflation-linked bonds showed a larger adjustment to real returns than to average inflation expectations. The ten-year real yield rose 6 basis points to 2.47%, the five-year 5 to 2.19%, and the 30-year 5 to 3.03%. Ten-year breakevens ended at 2.28%, up 1 basis point on the day and only 4 over July. The real yield rose 27 basis points over the month, accounting for most of the 31-basis-point nominal increase. Inflation concern remained, but the market was not pricing an equally large permanent increase in expected inflation.

Turnover was substantial. Treasury cash par volume reached $1.92 trillion, up 32.4%, and nominal-coupon activity rose 33.4% to $1.52 trillion. Seven-to-ten-year volume increased 56.4% to $279 billion, five-to-seven-year activity almost doubled to $173 billion, and TIPS volume rose 191% to $121.2 billion. These figures measure two-way trading rather than net flows, but place the benchmark and real-yield moves in an active market.

Late index-rebalancing demand trimmed intraday extremes after the 30-year reached 5.28%. The long-Treasury index still lost 0.69% on the day and 3.87% over July. One-to-three-year debt declined only 0.04% on Friday and retained a 0.17% monthly gain.

Investors also paid more for downside protection. The premium of one-month, 25-delta puts over calls reached its highest in about five months. Structures targeted ten-year yields around 4.8%–4.9% and 30-year yields around 5.3%–5.42%. MOVE remained comparatively subdued, making the costly downside skew more striking than the overall level of rates volatility.

The August-to-October refunding announcement was the next supply event. Auction sizes were expected to stay steady, with attention on guidance for possible coupon increases in 2027. Separately, Treasury was exploring investment of part of its near-$1 trillion cash balance in the roughly $13 trillion repo market. It could smooth pressures around settlements, tax dates and reporting periods if reserves declined, but operational demands, dealer-capacity concerns and modest estimated returns made adoption uncertain. That funding proposal would address cash-market fluctuations, not the additional duration investors might ultimately have to buy.

## Cable One and Extenet expose different weaknesses

Cable One's acquisition obligation was becoming harder to finance even at a discussed yield near 12%. The company needed roughly $1 billion for the mandatory purchase of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband Investments, after GTCR exercised a put, and to extend debt. Parts of Cable One's existing first-lien loan traded at yields near 18%.

Prospective lenders wanted ring-fencing to prevent the parent from subsidizing Mega Broadband's heavy obligations. Cable One already had at least $3 billion of long-term debt, limited free cash flow and competitive pressure in residential broadband. The central negotiation concerned whether new money could be insulated from the acquisition's liabilities, not just how much yield would attract buyers.

Extenet had moved beyond negotiating an extension to a missed payment. Interest due July 27 on about $500 million of asset-backed securities went unpaid. The payment administrator also reported that collections meant for bondholders had gone elsewhere and that some liens were no longer perfected. The company was negotiating interest forbearance, but the reported control failures raised questions about recovery as well as timing.

The cash deterioration was abrupt relative to operating revenue. Revenues had declined only slightly before Extenet warned in June that it was days from running out of cash. Fiber, small-cell and 5G structures had attracted buyers on the strength of infrastructure cash flows and security interests. Here, account administration and enforceable liens became at least as important as the growth outlook for digital connectivity.

Municipals faced a broader supply-and-duration problem. The index had lost 1.72% through Thursday, heading for its worst July since 2003 despite the coupon payments and redemptions that usually help summer demand. Issuance of roughly $47 billion exceeded the normal July pace just as long Treasury yields approached 19-year highs. Relative valuations became some of the cheapest of the year.

The calendar was still filling. Northwell Healthcare considered up to $800 million of tax-exempt bonds through New York's Dormitory Authority after hospital issuance had already reached about $26.7 billion year to date. The proposed sale would add another sizable test after a poor month, though its pricing and demand were still ahead.

The wider corporate supply backdrop also favored lenders. US junk issuance approached $200 billion for the year, about 9% above the same point in 2025, while high-grade supply increased by a third to $1.3 trillion. Average leveraged-loan prices fell from 97 in January to 95.3, with about $240 billion due through 2028. The higher margins and stronger protections accepted by CoreWeave and Proofpoint earlier in the week illustrated that broader change.

Energy producers were using the same commodity shock to reduce debt. Exxon cut net debt by more than $7 billion in the second quarter, Chevron directed a record $8.4 billion to debt reduction, and Shell reduced net debt about $10.8 billion. Cash flow was repairing those balance sheets while higher energy costs made financing harder elsewhere.

Broad credit returns held up relatively well. LQD lost 0.15%, HYG gained 0.01% and JNK 0.02%. Long AAA-to-A and BBB corporate indices declined 0.29% and 0.25%, less than the 0.69% long-Treasury loss, though their monthly declines remained 4.58% and 4.19%. The distinction between functioning markets and vulnerable individual structures remained important: neither a high coupon nor infrastructure collateral guaranteed access or recovery.

## Euro inflation rises and the BOJ makes later meetings live

Euro-area inflation accelerated from 2.8% to 2.9% in July, with energy up 10% and both services and the measure excluding food and fuel strengthening. German ten-year yields rose 1 basis point to 3.16%. Markets continued to assign a 90% chance to a quarter-point ECB increase in September and priced 42 basis points by year-end.

French data showed pressure beyond energy. Inflation rose to 2.4%, above every survey forecast and a 2.0% median; services accelerated from 1.9% to 2.3%. With euro-area second-quarter growth already twice expectations and the strongest in more than a year, the ECB faced less of a growth obstacle to further tightening.

The BOJ held 1% by an 8–1 vote after June's increase, but Kazuo Ueda made clear that meetings from September onward could bring action. Underlying inflation was nearing 2%, making upside surprises more costly, and he said the pace could accelerate if financial conditions remained too easy. Swaps put October hike odds at 89%. This kept an earlier move live without committing the bank to September.

Japan's data were mixed. Tokyo CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.9%, versus 1.8% expected; overall inflation and the measure excluding both fresh food and energy were 2%. Services edged up to 1.2%. June industrial output rose 1.3% from May, but retail sales fell 4.1% on the month and rose only 0.5% from a year earlier. The BOJ raised its fiscal-year growth forecast to 0.6% while lowering inflation from 2.8% to 2.5% because of subsidies.

Intervention bought time on the currency. Thursday's operation was estimated at JPY8.45 trillion, or $52.8 billion, and had lifted the yen as much as 3.3%. Friday brought reports of another operation, New York Fed rate checks and US Treasury coordination; the yen gained about 1.3% to 157.28. A firmer currency can ease imported inflation, but intervention and higher prospective domestic yields also affect the resources and incentives available for buying foreign bonds. A 1% BOJ rate remained far below the US range.

The UK's energy risks extended beyond the previous day's dovish guidance. BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill warned that commodity volatility could persist into 2027. The central forecast put inflation at a 3.2% late-year peak; an adverse scenario reached 4.5% in 2027 and required materially higher rates than the current 3.75%. Energy prices were already 20% above prewar levels. Resistance to an imminent increase did not remove that longer policy risk.

China's bond market was gaining a prospective hedging tool. Hong Kong prepared to relaunch five-year government-bond futures with a CNY500,000 cash-settled contract, after attempts in 2017 and 2024 failed to establish durable trading. Foreign holdings of onshore government debt had grown from about CNY450 billion in mid-2017 to CNY2 trillion. Sustained liquidity, rather than the launch alone, would determine whether investors could use the contract reliably for curve, basis and repo-linked strategies.

## Colombia pauses, while oil earnings leave Pemex dependent

Colombia surprised most economists by holding 12%. Of 27 surveyed, 23 had expected an increase; the board split four for a hold and three for a 50-basis-point hike. It also announced plans to accumulate as much as $4 billion of reserves. The peso's nearly 20% gain this year had reduced imported inflation and created room to wait, although reserve purchases could weaken that currency support.

Inflation remained above 6%, against a 3% target with a one-percentage-point tolerance band. Expansionary fiscal policy, a 23% minimum-wage rise and food and energy shocks kept pressure high, while the independent fiscal committee expected a deficit above 7% of GDP. Governor Leonardo Villar left further hikes open. The September meeting would test whether currency strength could keep offsetting those pressures under a new administration.

South African yields showed a partial recovery rather than a return to prewar conditions. The ten-year was around 8.7%, down from 9.5% early in the Iran war but above roughly 8% before it. The central bank had held 7% after a May increase provided room for patience. June inflation of 5% still exceeded the new 3% target, leaving the stance dependent on confidence that the shock would fade.

Pemex's better quarter had not restored financial independence. It reported MXN18 billion, or $1 billion, in profit and increased crude and condensate output 1.7% to 1.66 million barrels a day. Debt still stood at $77.5 billion. The government had budgeted $14 billion of debt support this year, while Fitch estimated a further $10 billion operating shortfall by year-end.

Mexico's finance minister ruled out additional state funds this year, even as Pemex discussed the 2027 budget and a possible refinancing. Production remained roughly half its historical peak and international partners were slow to commit. Higher oil improved cash generation without removing the potential financing burden on the state.

Market access also depended on operational rules. The Philippines planned to remove the effect of a 20% withholding tax from local-bond pricing ahead of expected JPMorgan index inclusion. The change would align its $230 billion market with global convention, but could create mark-to-market losses for holders selling before maturity.

India's index timetable moved the other way. Removing withholding and capital-gains taxes had attracted about $5 billion into eligible bonds since June 5, but Bloomberg deferred global aggregate inclusion because implementation was incomplete across investor regions. The ten-year yield rose 3 basis points to 6.84%, with traders expecting another 5–10 basis points of adjustment. Tax reform had brought inflows without securing immediate index entry.

Romania narrowly retained investment grade. Fitch affirmed BBB- with a negative outlook after an appeal and additional government information. The deficit was expected below 6% of GDP from more than 9% in 2024, but political uncertainty and the 2028 election cycle threatened further consolidation. The rating preserved access without removing the fiscal warning.

EMB fell 0.14% and the 15-year-plus dollar sovereign index 0.21%, while the dollar index slipped 0.21% to 99.80. Currency conditions were not signaling a general dollar shortage, but the 4.75% ten-year Treasury and 5.27% long bond still raised the discount applied to long hard-currency cash flows.

## Stocks advance despite the rate shock

The S&P 500 gained 0.70%, the Nasdaq 100 0.60% and VIX fell 6.44% to 15.99. Semiconductors edged up only 0.07%, remaining down 4.30% over the week and 20.61% over the month. Broader risk appetite was intact, even though the AI complex had yet to recover convincingly from doubts over spending returns.

WTI and Brent rose 1.29% and 1.22%, to $84.67 and $90.12. Both were lower over the week but more than 21% higher over a month. The oil increase added to the inflation backdrop, while the much larger rise in real yields showed that it was not the whole Treasury story.

Gold declined 1.24% to $4,049.10 and the dollar index fell to 99.80, partly as action supported the yen. With gold and volatility lower and equities higher, the day did not resemble a wholesale loss of confidence. Investors were repricing real duration and policy uncertainty while equity and credit trading continued to function.

## Payrolls and refunding set the next US tests

The August 7 employment report follows the 0.9% employment-cost reading. The survey median expects 85,000 new jobs after 57,000 in June and unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. Stronger hiring would support the dissenters' concern that policy is insufficiently restrictive; weaker employment and softer subsequent prices would strengthen the case for patience. Real yields will show whether any relief extends beyond a decline in inflation compensation.

The August-to-October refunding announcement separates supply expectations from the Fed debate. Auction sizes were expected to remain steady, with the key question whether guidance postpones increases or prepares investors for larger 2027 issuance. Hedging around 4.9% in ten-year yields and 5.3%–5.42% at 30 years provides a reference for how investors are protecting against an earlier supply signal. Treasury's possible repo investment operates on a different horizon: it could smooth settlement-related funding, not solve coupon absorption.

August euro-area inflation will show whether July's 10% energy rise is spreading further into services before September's ECB meeting. The BOJ's September 18 decision will follow a test of whether yen stability can last without repeated intervention or another disorderly JGB move. In credit, Cable One's next financing terms, Northwell's proposed municipal sale and subsequent AI or software deals will show how far concession and enforceable protections can sustain access. Delays or further demands for ring-fencing would indicate that high real rates are reaching more borrowers, even without a broad funding stop.
